role_line.text: Climate activist and education reformer; fasted 26 days in support of the CJP protest
role_line.note: First half is The Quint's descriptor ('Climate activist and education reformer'); '26-day fast in support of students' is Quint/TNM wording. Alternative verbatim from Al Jazeera 14 Jul: 'an engineer-turned-activist who inspired a character in the blockbuster Bollywood film, 3 Idiots'. Fetch tool paraphrased Quint page, so re-check exact descriptor wording before locking.

facts.claim: Wangchuk had called himself an 'honorary cockroach' BEFORE the street protest (PTI, 23 May 2026); said he does not qualify as a member because he is not jobless or idle
facts.headline: Sonam Wangchuk calls himself 'honorary cockroach', urges govt to hear voices of youth
facts.snippet: But I consider myself an honorary cockroach,

facts.claim: Wangchuk attended/joined the CJP protest at Jantar Mantar on Sat 6 Jun; said he doesn't like protests but felt compelled over students' concerns
facts.headline: 'I Don't Like Protests, But We Need Justice': Sonam Wangchuk Joins CJP Rally at Jantar Mantar
facts.snippet: I don't like protests, but we have to do it for justice,

facts.headline: Students, Activists Rally at Jantar Mantar as Sonam Wangchuk Joins Protest
facts.snippet: Sonam Wangchuk on Saturday joined a protest at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi organised by the Cockroach Janata Party

facts.claim: Fast began 28 Jun with six AISA students at the CJP protest site (Wire does not name Neha or Hamad)
facts.headline: In Photos: Sonam Wangchuk, Left Students Go on Hunger Strike at CJP's Jantar Mantar Protest
facts.snippet: six students from the All India Students' Association (AISA)

facts.claim: Hunger strike since 28 Jun; names AISA strikers Neha Bora, Manish Kumar, Aameen Amitosh; a CJP spokesperson's post adds Hamad (so 'independent student Hamad' not confirmed; 3 or 4 named, not 6)
facts.headline: CJP protest: Police force Sonam Wangchuk into hospital, Dipke begins indefinite hunger strike
facts.snippet: Wangchuk had been on hunger strike since June 28.

facts.claim: Why he fasts: backing CJP founder Dipke's demand that Education Minister Pradhan resign over exam paper leaks; 17th day on 14 Jul; CJP said 8.5 kg lost
facts.headline: Indian activist Wangchuk urged to end hunger strike over exam paper leaks
facts.snippet: an engineer-turned-activist who inspired a character in the blockbuster Bollywood film, 3 Idiots

facts.claim: 1,800+ civil society members urged him to end fast (released Tue 14 Jul, day 17)
facts.headline: CJP protest: Over 1,800 civil society members urge Sonam Wangchuk to end hunger strike
facts.snippet: More than 1,800 members of civil society on Tuesday urged activist Sonam Wangchuk to withdraw his hunger strike in Delhi.

facts.claim: Weight loss: more than nine kg by day 19 (Thu 16 Jul); doctor warned organs could be affected
facts.headline: Sonam Wangchuk loses over 9 kg after 19 days of hunger strike; doctors warn it could affect organs
facts.snippet: The next stage can be alarming. Organs can be impacted.

facts.claim: Exact figure 9.1 kg appears in BBC copy (not a preferred outlet; use only as backup)
facts.headline: Indian activist urged to end hunger strike as he loses 9.1kg in 19 days
facts.snippet: has lost 9.1kg and aides say he's in immense pain

facts.claim: 18 Jul: police removed him from Jantar Mantar to Safdarjung; police: 'essential medical care'; CJP said he had been 'detained'
facts.headline: CJP protest: Police force Sonam Wangchuk into hospital, Dipke begins indefinite hunger strike

facts.claim: CJP used 'kidnapped'; Newslaundry says police 'forcibly removed' him
facts.headline: Sonam Wangchuk forcibly taken to hospital as Delhi Police tighten grip on Jantar Mantar protest
facts.snippet: he has been forcefully kidnapped by the Police and taken away.

facts.claim: Police statement cited HC order; protester says 'like a kidnapping'; article calls it 'early-morning detention'
facts.headline: 'Like a kidnapping': How Delhi Police forced Sonam Wangchuk out of Jantar Mantar
facts.snippet: They shielded him and took him away just like a kidnapping.

facts.claim: 21 Jul: Delhi HC division bench ordered immediate shift from Safdarjung to Medanta; Centre had no objection
facts.headline: Sonam Wangchuk shifted from Safdarjung Hospital to Medanta after Delhi HC order
facts.snippet: we direct that Sonam Wangchuk be shifted immediately to Medanta Hospital,

facts.claim: 22 Jul: he sought a written assurance from the Centre before ending fast
facts.headline: Sonam Wangchuk Seeks Written Govt Assurance Before Ending 25-Day Hunger Strike
facts.snippet: receiving a written assurance from the Centre.

facts.claim: Fast ended after 26 days at Medanta in presence of Nadda and Jitendra Singh; Scroll says on 'Friday' (24 Jul)
facts.headline: Activist Sonam Wangchuk ends fast after 26 days, CJP says protest to continue till Pradhan resigns
facts.snippet: in the presence of Union ministers Jitendra Singh and JP Nadda.

facts.claim: Ended 'past midnight on Friday, July 24'; assurance 'read out by' Nadda (does not say written); Dipke: protest continues
facts.headline: Fast ends, protest doesn't: CJP to continue agitation after Wangchuk ends strike
facts.snippet: We are relieved and grateful that Sonam sir has ended his hunger strike after 26 days.

facts.claim: Ministers delivered written assurances in person; ended 'shortly after midnight on Friday'
facts.headline: Why Did Sonam Wangchuk End His Hunger Strike? What The Centre Promised And What Comes Next

facts.claim: The Week: ended 'Thursday night' (meeting ~12:30 am); government gave written assurances; three promises
facts.headline: PM Modi's video, Nadda's visit, 3 key promises: Behind Sonam Wangchuk's decision to end his hunger strike
facts.snippet: indefinite hunger strike on Thursday night

facts.claim: Govt assurance: no cases against peaceful Jantar Mantar protesters
facts.headline: Wangchuk ends 26-day fast following govt assurance; CJP to continue protest
facts.snippet: The government is positive on not registering cases against those protesting peacefully at Jantar Mantar in Delhi.

disagreements: CLIENT SUMMARY: 'detained and carried away when he started his hunger strike' does not fit the start. He started the fast voluntarily on 28 Jun (Wire, Scroll, Al Jazeera). The removal was 18 Jul, day 21, nearly three weeks later. The fast then continued in hospital.

'Detained': police never use it (they say 'essential medical care', shifted). CJP said he was 'detained' (Scroll 18 Jul) and 'forcefully kidnapped' (Newslaundry). Newslaundry/TNM narrative says 'early-morning detention'. Scroll/Newslaundry/Wire say 'forcibly removed'. DT Next (PTI) says 'shifted'. No outlet says 'carried away'. Suggest 'removed by police' with claimant attribution.

Ledger 'kidnapping' attribution: Scroll 18 Jul quotes CJP as 'detained' not 'kidnapping'; 'kidnapped' is in Newslaundry's quoted CJP statement; 'like a kidnapping' is a protester (Vikas Kumar), not CJP official.

End date: ledger says 23 Jul. Scroll, TNM, Outlook, Quint, DT Next put it Friday 24 Jul (shortly after midnight); The Week says 'Thursday night' (meeting ~12:30 am). '26 days' only works counting 28 Jun to 23 Jul inclusive, so 23 Jul (Thursday night) vs 24 Jul (just after midnight). Recommend 'night of 23-24 Jul'.

'Written assurances': Outlook and The Week say written. Scroll, Quint, DT Next, TNM say assurances were conveyed/read out by Nadda without saying 'written'. Wangchuk demanded written assurance on 22 Jul (FPJ). A LatestLY/ANI headline quotes 'Given Written Assurances' (not fetched).
1,800+ signatories: Scroll dates the letter Tue 14 Jul (day 17), not ~17 Jul. The Wire counts 1,821 (not fetched in full). A separate ~60-person appeal came on day 20 (Outlook/Quint/TNM).

Weight: 9.1 kg is BBC (16 Jul, day 19, via a non-preferred mirror); DT Next/Deccan Herald say 'more than nine kg'; CJP said 8.5 kg on 14 Jul (Al Jazeera); doctors later cited about 11 kg (search summary, unverified). Ledger 'about 17 Jul' is day 20; reports are 16 Jul.

6 Jun vs 28 Jun: FPJ and Kashmir Life say he joined the CJP protest on 6 Jun; Brut and DT Next say he 'joined' on 28 Jun. Al Jazeera's own 6 Jun report does not mention him. Both are consistent if 6 Jun was a visit and 28 Jun the fast.
'Honorary cockroach' dates to 23 May (PTI), before the protest and before 6 Jun; Britannica repeats it.

Fast companions: Wire says six AISA students; Scroll names three (Neha Bora, Manish Kumar, Aameen Amitosh) plus Hamad in a CJP post. 'Independent student Hamad' and 'Neha Bora' with six-total are not confirmed in one page; Wire photo piece does not name them.
Britannica says he fasted 20 days before removal and that ministers met him 'at the hospital' on day 26; consistent with 21st day on 18 Jul but Britannica/Wikipedia are not news sources.

Not found in any fetched outlet: Wangchuk described as 'honorary cockroach' in July coverage; 'detained' in Scroll 24 Jul or Quint or Outlook end-of-fast pieces. Not fetched/verified: Hindu, HT, NDTV, Indian Express (searches did not surface them; Business Standard returned 403; Deccan Herald 403). Wire pages often returned only headlines.
